submissions.findingTextShort: ONTRAC found fewer new nonmelanoma skin cancers during treatment in immunocompetent adults at high prior skin-cancer risk.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The ONTRAC phase-3 double-blind randomized trial in 386 immunocompetent adults with at least two prior nonmelanoma skin cancers found oral nicotinamide 500 mg twice daily for 12 months reduced the rate of new nonmelanoma skin cancers during treatment; the effect did not persist after supplementation stopped and must remain a secondary-prevention result for a specifically high-risk dermatology population.
submissions.populationContext: Immunocompetent adults with at least two nonmelanoma skin cancers in the previous five years
submissions.usageContext: Nicotinamide 500 mg twice daily for 12 months
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Do not generalize this to healthy low-risk users, generic cancer prevention, or benefit after discontinuation.

submissions.findingTextShort: A phase-3 transplant-recipient trial using the same 500-mg twice-daily regimen found no keratinocyte-cancer prevention benefit.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A phase-3 placebo-controlled trial in 158 immunosuppressed solid-organ transplant recipients using nicotinamide 500 mg twice daily for 12 months found no reduction in keratinocyte cancers, squamous-cell carcinoma, basal-cell carcinoma, actinic keratoses, or quality-of-life outcomes; the trial stopped early for poor recruitment, but its population-specific null result must remain alongside ONTRAC.
submissions.populationContext: Immunosuppressed solid-organ transplant recipients at high skin-cancer risk
submissions.usageContext: Nicotinamide 500 mg twice daily for 12 months
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Population biology and early stopping limit simple cross-population conclusions; this does not erase ONTRAC and ONTRAC does not erase this null trial.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2022 meta-analysis favored nicotinamide for selected skin-cancer outcomes but only supported a weak, population-specific recommendation.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 randomized trials involving 3,039 patients found pooled skin-cancer outcomes that favored nicotinamide in selected contexts, but heterogeneity and risk-of-bias concerns led to only a weak recommendation with moderate-quality evidence for selected high-risk populations rather than broad chemoprevention.
submissions.populationContext: High-risk and other clinical populations across 29 randomized trials
submissions.usageContext: Nicotinamide interventions with heterogeneous dermatologic outcomes
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Pooled synthesis must retain population and outcome heterogeneity and cannot become generic cancer-prevention marketing.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2024 meta-analysis pooling immunocompetent and immunosuppressed populations did not find statistically significant overall NMSC prevention estimates.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2024 meta-analysis focused on nonmelanoma skin-cancer chemoprevention reported that pooled estimates for squamous-cell carcinoma, basal-cell carcinoma, and overall nonmelanoma skin cancer were not statistically significant after combining immunocompetent and immunosuppressed populations; this is an important contradiction/heterogeneity signal rather than proof that every subgroup lacks benefit.
submissions.populationContext: Mixed immunocompetent and immunosuppressed high-risk populations
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Pooling biologically distinct populations may obscure subgroup-specific effects; preserve the primary randomized trials separately.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2024 clinical-trial report documents drug-induced liver injury during 3-g/day nicotinamide exposure.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2024 report from a glaucoma neuroprotection clinical trial documented drug-induced liver injury during pharmacologic nicotinamide exposure of 3 grams per day; this provides form-specific evidence that high-dose nicotinamide can cause clinically important hepatotoxicity and should not be conflated with nicotinic-acid flushing or treated as risk-free because it is non-flushing.
submissions.usageContext: Pharmacologic nicotinamide exposure at 3 grams per day
submissions.safetyContext: Direct high-dose liver-injury signal for nicotinamide itself.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This does not define incidence or risk at nutritional or lower supplemental doses.
